title: Bag of Tricks or Bag of Myths? Reducing Modeling Complexity with Task Knowledge in Explainable Suicide Risk Assessment
abstract: arXiv:2609.07766v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Assessing suicide risk from social media text is a small-data, high-stakes setting requiring not only severity prediction but also supporting evidence and clinically relevant risk and protective factors. Yet common NLP techniques, including model scaling, synthetic data, loss reweighting, ensembling, and threshold tuning, are often applied without testing whether their gains hold up under severe class imbalance, coupled outputs, and limited author-level data. We study 1,635 clinician-annotated posts and audit 31 pre-specified techniques from 7 methodological families through roughly 300 controlled experiments on author-disjoint partitions. We found no prior audit of this playbook in this regime. The findings guide a task-grounded system for three outputs: 4-level suicide risk, evidence spans, and 24 clinical risk and protective factors. Only 5 of 31 comparisons produced reliable gains. We reformulate factor prediction as entailment bet

translated_title: 《技巧之袋还是迷思之袋？在可解释的自杀风险评估中利用任务知识降低建模复杂度》
translated_abstract: 从社交媒体文本中评估自杀风险是一个小数据、高风险的场景，不仅需要预测严重程度，还需要提供支持证据以及临床相关的风险和保护因素。然而，常见的NLP技术，包括模型扩展、合成数据、损失重加权、集成学习和阈值调整，通常在未经检验的情况下被应用，没有验证它们的收益在严重类别不平衡、耦合输出和有限的作者级数据条件下是否依然成立。我们研究了1,635条临床医生标注的帖子，并通过在作者不相交的划分上进行的约300个受控实验，审计了来自7个方法论家族的31种预先指定的技术。我们发现在这一场景中尚无对此类方法手册的先前审计。研究结果指导了一个面向任务的系统，该系统提供三种输出：4级自杀风险、证据跨度和24个临床风险与保护因素。31项比较中仅有5项产生了可靠的收益。我们将因素预测重新表述为蕴含任务……
tldr: 该论文通过约300个受控实验审计了31种常见NLP技巧在可解释自杀风险评估中的真实有效性，发现仅有5种产生可靠收益，并提出利用任务知识（如将因素预测重构为蕴含任务）来简化建模复杂度。
en_tdlr: Through roughly 300 controlled experiments auditing 31 common NLP techniques for explainable suicide risk assessment, this paper finds that only 5 produce reliable gains and proposes reducing modeling complexity with task knowledge, such as reformulating factor prediction as entailment.
